Goal: Attendees find the app pleasant and worth using rather than a chore
Metric: Average app star rating (1-5); count of ratings submitted
Hypotheses: 4.0+ suggests the app earned its place. Below 3.5 suggests it added friction rather than removing it. Very few ratings at all is itself a signal - people rate what they care about.

Goal: Attendees can tell speakers what landed
Metric: Average session star rating; % of rated sessions with a written comment
Hypotheses: Comments on more than a quarter of ratings suggests people felt heard. Ratings clustered on a few sessions suggests only strong reactions get recorded.

Goal: The directory helps people meet the right person
Hypotheses: Above 20% suggests the directory is doing its job as an introduction. Very low suggests people browse but do not act.

Goal: Attendees follow what is happening during the day
Signals: Feed opened; post read; new-posts banner tapped
Metric: Feed views per attendee per day; median time between feed opens during event hours
Hypotheses: Several opens per attendee suggests the feed became the reflex for 'what is going on'. One or two suggests it was checked once and forgotten.

Goal: Attendees contribute and not only consume
Metric: Attendee posts / attendees who signed in
Hypotheses: Above 10% would be strong for a one-day event. Near zero suggests opening the feed was the wrong call, or people did not realise they could.

Goal: Attendees plan their day rather than drifting
Metric: Attendees with 1+ starred session / total signed in; median stars per planner
Hypotheses: Above 40% suggests planning is a real need. Below 15% suggests the programme is small enough to hold in your head.

Goal: Open Sessions stay current without organiser effort
Metric: Scans published per day; corrections applied per scan
Hypotheses: More than one correction per scan on average means the reading is not trusted and the flow costs more than it saves.

Goal: Ticket holders actually get into the app
Hypotheses: Above 60% would be a strong result for an optional event app. Below 30% points at the email or the on-ramp rather than the app.

Goal: Attendees keep the app to hand
Signals: PWA installed; launched from home screen
Hypotheses: Above 30% suggests the install prompt worked. Low install rate caps notification reach on iOS, so this and notification opt-in should move together.

Goal: Attendees opt in to being told things
Hypotheses: Above 50% suggests asking after profile setup was right. Well below suggests the ask came at the wrong moment, or iOS install got in the way.

Goal: Attendees accept the profile made for them
Metric: Attendees who edited a prefilled profile / signed-in attendees
Hypotheses: High editing suggests the prefilled data was wrong. Low editing with high directory use suggests we got it right first time.

Goal: Attendees come back through the day rather than once
Metric: Attendees active in 3+ distinct hours / signed-in attendees
Hypotheses: Above 50% suggests the app is part of the day rather than a novelty at registration.
Above 20% suggests announcements are useful. Very low suggests they are noise and the kill switch should have been used.

Goal: The app is still useful after the event
Metric: Attendees active on day+1 / signed-in attendees
Hypotheses: Any meaningful figure suggests slides and the directory have a life beyond the day, which would justify keeping it live.

Goal: Getting in is not a barrier
Signals: Sign-in started; sign-in completed; sign-in error
Hypotheses: Below 90% is a problem. Every failure at this step is a person who never sees anything else.

Goal: Attendees find the session they are looking for
Hypotheses: A high ratio suggests the list is scannable and the tap targets are right.

Signals: Directory search; profile opened from a search
Metric: Profile opens from search / searches performed
Hypotheses: Above 50% suggests search works. Low suggests the name folding or the ordering is wrong.

Goal: A photo becomes a correct schedule without a fight
Signals: Scan started; scan published; scan discarded
Hypotheses: Above 70% suggests the reading is good enough to trust. Frequent discards mean the model is not earning its place.

Goal: Attendees get the deck they wanted
Signals: Slides announcement posted; slides download tapped
Hypotheses: Above 25% suggests the auto-posting is well timed. Low suggests attendees had already left or did not notice.
